transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I feel like I just cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. Everything just ends up in piles. Like, my supplies, due dates, receipts, and my assignment notes... they all just pile up everywhere, and I look at it and I really don't know what to do first.
Have you struggled with this level of disorganization your entire life, or is this something that has started more recently?

It's more recent, actually. Um, I'd say it's been a real problem for about two years and two months now. That's when I changed schools. I had to start managing the new business program along with my accessories shop, and there was just... a lot less structure for me to rely on.
Over the past two years, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I get stressed out and frustrated about the mess and falling behind, but I don't feel depressed or hopeless. I'm actually pretty upbeat most of the time, just... overwhelmed by everything I need to do.
Looking back at your childhood, before this transition two years ago, did you frequently struggle with staying organized, following instructions, or sitting still in school?

Yeah, I definitely struggled with sitting still. Um, my mom actually still has some of my old notes from elementary school teachers. They basically said I was always getting out of my seat and talking before being called on. I also used to just rush through all our group activities, even when I totally understood the work. I just couldn't really slow down or stay put.
